messages:
sophia: Heads-up — team wants to onboard a community model called zephyr-14b. Before we spin up evaluation infra, can legal/compliance confirm any nonstandard restrictions?

alex: quick context: zephyr-14b is weight release from a public repo, claims permissive license in README but there's a separate LICENSE.pdf attached. We want to test int8/4-bit quant, run in Dedicated, and maybe offer as a catalog model with a warning tag.

jordan-legal: Can you paste the exact license text? sometimes repos include a compatibility note in LICENSE.pdf that differs from README.

sophia: pasted the header from LICENSE.pdf below:

```
This model is provided under the Zephyr Community License v1.0.
Permission is granted for research and internal business use only. Commercial redistribution, resale, or providing model weights as a service is prohibited without a separate commercial license from the authors. Derivative model weights (including fine-tuned or quantized redistributions) are not allowed to be redistributed.
Export restrictions: no export to countries/actors on applicable sanctions lists.
```

alex: ok so two flags: (1) "internal business use only" — unclear if hosting as a customer-facing hosted API counts as prohibited; (2) explicit ban on redistribution of derivative weights (that could block us from storing or serving quantized weights to customers).

mike-compliance: That wording is restrictive. "Internal business use only" usually allows using model internally (prod features behind our product for our customers might be a gray area). "Providing model weights as a service" seems to target model marketplaces. But the derivative/quantized redistribution clause is explicit — if taken literally, we cannot share quantized weights outside our org. Serving generated text might be ok, but offering downloadable weights or embedding the weights into a private package for customers could violate it.

jordan-legal: My read: (a) Hosted inference (we serve completions via API) is likely allowed as "internal business use" if we are using the model to power our own product (but not reselling the weights as a standalone artifact). (b) Dedicated or Private: if a customer-managed Private deployment would involve delivering weights to the customer environment, that could be considered redistribution and be prohibited. (c) Quantization: creating quantized weights is a derivative; redistributing quantized files is prohibited unless we secure a commercial license.

irina-ops: Practically, this blocks offering zephyr-14b in Redwood Private (customer gets the weights) and blocks exposing quantized weight files for download. We can still run hosted inference in our cloud if legal signs off. Need to know if we can cache KV/prefixes and persist them — those are not model weights but derived state.

jordan-legal: Good point — cached KV/prefix matrices are ephemeral runtime state; license seems focused on weights redistribution. Still, we should avoid packaging or exporting any trained weights or converted/quantized checkpoints.

legal-bot: License red flags detected: derivative redistribution prohibition; export control clause; ambiguous "internal business use". Recommend: get explicit written permission from model authors for hosting & quantization.

sophia: Next steps proposed: 1) Add zephyr-14b to intake queue with "restricted-hosting" flag. 2) Run evals (safety, quality, latency) in isolated infra, not sharing weights. 3) Ask legal to request a commercial/hosting license from upstream authors. 4) Block catalog listing until permission is obtained. 5) If authors grant permission, ensure contract includes permission to create and redistribute quantized weights and permit Dedicated/Private deployments. Does that capture everyone?

alex: captures it. Also add a technical checklist for the eval run: - run quantization experiments but keep quantized artifacts local to ephemeral nodes, no S3 persist; - run evaluation harness with redwood/evals; - collect token-level cost/latency profiles to check perf impact.

mike-compliance: Add export control screening step: verify that authors are not in sanctioned jurisdictions and that the model training data or intended use doesn't create additional export concerns. Also document provenance (training data sources) in the intake form.

jordan-legal: I'll draft an email template to request a hosting/redistribution addendum from the authors. Template will ask for: explicit permission for hosting as API, permission to produce/distribute quantized weights, permission to allow Dedicated/Private deployments, and confirmation about export restrictions.

irina-ops: Operational note — if we get permission to host but not to redistribute quantized checkpoints, we can still run quantized in-host for inference but must ensure no snapshot of quantized files are accessible or downloadable. We should add runtime auditing to detect any unintended file exposure.

sophia: ok thanks. I'll flag this model as "license-review" in the intake board and attach these notes. Jordan, ping when the email template is ready and we'll send it.

jordan-legal: Template ready, sharing in #legal-templates in 30m. If authors respond positively, we can move to cataloging and a limited canary for hosted inference under legal-approved terms.

alex: tiny follow-up — do we want to attempt a patent check? the license doesn't mention patents but some community models include patent grants elsewhere.

jordan-legal: Good call — I'll add a patent clause check to the intake checklist.

sophia: thanks all. marking thread resolved for now, will reopen once author reply arrives. :thumbsup:
